title: Vendor Risk Questionnaire Walkthrough - Acme Financial
next_steps: Redwood to upload SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestations to shared portal by 2025-02-18
Priya (Acme) to send the customer SIG/CAIQ PDF to Redwood and flag high-priority questions by 2025-02-17
Schedule follow-up call for evidence review and remediation plan week of 2025-02-24
Redwood SE to provide KMS architecture diagram and key rotation policy by 2025-02-20
action_items: Alex Moreno - Upload SOC2 and ISO evidence to Acme secure portal - 2025-02-18
Priya Nair - Prepare KMS_architecture_diagram.pdf and encryption summary - 2025-02-20
Jordan Blake - Compile RBAC/SSO config export and sample audit logs - 2025-02-20
Mark Ortiz - Share specific SIG questions that are blocker for procurement - 2025-02-17
summary: Walkthrough of Acme Financial vendor risk questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ). Covered SOC 2 and ISO attestations, RBAC and SSO integration (SAML/Okta), audit logging and retention, data residency options for EU, encryption at rest/in transit and KMS integration, and evidence delivery process. Agreed next steps for sharing reports and scheduling follow-up evidence review.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestations
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
transcript: 00:00 Alex Moreno: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, Alex from Redwood here with Priya our SE and Jordan from security
00:07 Dana Li: Thanks, Dana here, CISO at Acme Financial, Priya from our vendor risk team will co-run questions
00:13 Priya Sharma: yeah hi all, we sent over the SIG/CAIQ earlier, want to walk through the high-risk items and evidence requests
00:20 Priya Nair: Great, thanks, we pulled the PDF and we'll go section by section and note where we can provide attestations vs config screenshots
00:28 Mark Ortiz: Quick note on time, some of our legal folks may ask about data residency, especially EU processing — we need clarity on that
00:37 Alex Moreno: Absolutely — we'll cover region controls, dedicated vs hosted options, and private deployment for EU-only processing
00:44 Speaker 1: (mumble) ok good
00:56 Priya Nair: Starting with SOC 2, we have a current Type II report for the 2024 period, scope covers hosted API and control plane, not customer-managed private infra
01:10 Dana Li: Is the SOC 2 scope audited for encryption key management where Redwood manages keys?

01:16 Jordan Blake: Good question — our SOC scope includes our key management processes where we manage keys in our hosted offering, but for Private deployments customers manage KMS and that scope is different
01:26 Priya Sharma: Can you provide the SOC 2 report redacted? we need the attestation and testing procedures
01:31 Alex Moreno: Yes we'll upload the redacted SOC 2 Type II report to the secure portal, link and access by 2/18. We'll also include the SOC 2 bridge letter for any recent changes
01:41 Mark Ortiz: Great. For ISO, do you have an ISO 27001 cert and scope?
01:46 Jordan Blake: We have ISO 27001 cert covering our control plane and development org, we'll attach the cert pdf and scope statement
01:53 Priya Nair: Moving to SIG/CAIQ controls — many of the questions are about encryption at rest and in transit, can you summarise cipher suites and TLS versions supported?
02:02 Alex Moreno: We default to TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred, cipher suites are industry standard ECDHE-based, and we can provide a config excerpt for endpoints
02:11 Dana Li: On encryption at rest, who manages keys? we need KMS integration details and rotation cadence

02:17 Jordan Blake: For hosted customers we offer two models: Redwood-managed KMS (we use cloud KMS with strict controls) or customer-managed keys via BYOK in their cloud. Rotation policy is 90 days for symmetric keys, and we can share the key rotation policy doc
02:28 Priya Sharma: Does Redwood support HSM-backed keys? Some of our systems require HSM-level protection
02:33 Priya Nair: Yes, we integrate with customer HSM/KMS providers and support HSM-backed keys in the Dedicated/Private models — we'll include the integration notes
02:42 Mark Ortiz: Ok noted — you mentioned audit logs earlier, what's the retention and format for logs?

02:48 Jordan Blake: By default we retain audit logs for 90 days in hosted; enterprise customers can request longer retention up to 7 years as an add-on. Logs are delivered in JSON with structured event types and can be exported to customer SIEM via S3 or streaming connectors
02:59 Dana Li: Are logs tamper-evident? do you support WORM or signed logs?
03:05 Jordan Blake: We provide append-only storage and can support signed log feeds and WORM in Dedicated setups; we'll include a sample audit log and schema in the portal
03:14 Priya Sharma: About RBAC — how granular are roles and can you sync groups from Okta?
03:20 Priya Nair: We offer role-based access with predefined roles and custom roles, and full SCIM group sync from Okta/SAML SSO. We'll provide a config export showing the RBAC role table
03:30 Mark Ortiz: For SSO, does Redwood support SAML, OIDC, Okta? any known gotchas?

03:35 Alex Moreno: SAML and OIDC supported, Okta is the most common IdP. Gotchas: provisioning vs just SSO — if you need SCIM provisioning to auto-assign roles we can enable it but it requires a service account and permissions on the IdP side
03:47 Dana Li: Data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of workloads. Can Redwood guarantee that?

03:53 Priya Nair: For Hosted we can pin workloads to EU regions and limit egress. For the strictest requirement we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment so control plane and data plane are entirely in-customer region — we'll outline options
04:05 Priya Sharma: Ok can you provide an architecture diagram for EU-only flow?
04:10 Jordan Blake: Yes Jordan will prepare a EU-dataflow-diagram and the configuration checklist
04:16 Alex Moreno: We'll also call out where metadata may still transit control plane services depending on the deployment mode
04:23 Speaker 2: (crosstalk) yeah
04:35 Priya Nair: Procurement often asks about subcontractors and subprocessors — we keep a list of subprocessors and will share the latest registry
04:41 Mark Ortiz: Do subprocessors have SOC reports as well?
04:45 Jordan Blake: Major cloud providers used by Redwood do have attestations; we'll provide the subprocessor list and their certifications where available
04:53 Dana Li: Regarding SIG, some questions are very prescriptive about change control and vulnerability management — do you have evidence for patch timelines and vulnerability scanning?

05:00 Jordan Blake: We run regular vulnerability scanning and monthly patch windows for infra, critical security patches are applied as needed. We'll share summary reports and our vuln management policy
05:10 Priya Sharma: Evidence requests will likely include sample change tickets and proof of remediation timelines, is that available?
05:15 Alex Moreno: Yes we can provide redacted change tickets and a sample remediation report, we'll coordinate on redaction needs
05:24 Mark Ortiz: On encryption again — for customer-managed keys, is plaintext ever accessible to Redwood support?
05:30 Jordan Blake: No, with BYOK and customer-managed keys we do not have access to plaintext; the keys are never exported to Redwood's control plane in that model
05:38 Dana Li: For Dedicated deployments, can you host the control plane in our VPC?
05:43 Priya Nair: We offer a private control plane option and a full on-prem package for air-gapped environments; there are tradeoffs around updates and support SLAs which we can discuss
05:53 Priya Sharma: About the SIG matrix: are there any known gaps we should expect so we can prepare compensating controls?
05:59 Jordan Blake: A couple of low-level operational items like default log retention and long-term archive are configurable but may need add-ons; we'll call those out in the answers
06:08 Alex Moreno: We'll mark any question where evidence is only available for Dedicated/Private and propose compensating controls for hosted customers
06:16 Dana Li: How do you handle customer data deletion requests and proof of deletion?

06:21 Jordan Blake: We have documented data retention and deletion workflows; for hosted we can provide deletion logs and snapshots of deletion activity, for private customers they control the storage lifecycle
06:30 Mark Ortiz: Legal may ask for a Data Processing Agreement and SCCs for EU customers
06:35 Alex Moreno: We have a standard DPA and incorporate SCCs where required; we'll share the DPA draft in the portal
06:43 Priya Sharma: For the questionnaire, we'd like the SIG answers pre-populated where possible, can Redwood provide a filled CAIQ spreadsheet?
06:49 Priya Nair: Yes we typically populate the CAIQ and attach supporting docs. We'll return a filled CAIQ and a mapping to evidence artifacts
07:00 Dana Li: Can the evidence artifacts be uploaded to a secure portal or do you prefer email?
07:05 Alex Moreno: We prefer the secure portal (we'll send an invite), but can also provide s3 links with short-lived tokens if needed
07:12 Priya Sharma: Ok portal access for our team please, we need at least two reviewers to have read-only access
07:18 Alex Moreno: Noted — we'll grant read-only to Dana and Priya, and a separate access for Mark for log samples
07:26 Speaker 3: (typing)
07:40 Mark Ortiz: A couple technical clarifications — do you expose KV cache state or model weights in logs?
07:46 Priya Nair: No logs do not contain model weights or KV cache contents; we redact any sensitive payloads and provide schema for event types
07:55 Dana Li: Are you able to provide pen test reports?
07:59 Jordan Blake: We do annual third-party pen tests and will share redacted executive summaries and remediation attestations
08:07 Priya Sharma: In SIG there is a question about business continuity and DR — what are your RTO/RPO commitments?
08:13 Alex Moreno: For hosted we publish SLA and typical RTOs; for enterprise Dedicated we can agree to stricter RTO/RPO in the contract. We'll add the SLA binder
08:22 Mark Ortiz: For procurement timeline, we typically need the filled CAIQ, SOC 2, ISO, and log samples before formal approval — can we get those within two weeks?
08:29 Alex Moreno: Yes target two weeks for the core artifacts, then follow-up for remaining items
08:36 Priya Sharma: How will you handle redactions for tickets and logs to avoid exposing customer data?
08:42 Jordan Blake: We'll redact PII and provide a redaction log describing what was removed, and maintain original evidence in our secure evidence store for auditors
08:52 Dana Li: If we want to scope only certain product surfaces, can we narrow the CAIQ answers?
08:58 Priya Nair: Absolutely, we'll map each SIG response to product scope — hosted API, Dedicated, Private — and mark N/A where not in scope
09:08 Mark Ortiz: Any limitations on long-term archival for logs if we ask for 7-year retention?
09:13 Jordan Blake: Technical capacity supported, may be an add-on and involves storage costs; we'll provide pricing estimates in the portal
09:21 Alex Moreno: Quick recap before we wrap — we'll upload SOC2/ISO certs, a filled CAIQ, KMS architecture diagram, sample audit logs and RBAC export, and invite you to the secure portal
09:31 Dana Li: That sounds good, last question — do you have insurance certificates (cyber liability)?
09:36 Jordan Blake: Yes we carry cyber insurance, certificate will be uploaded as part of the attestations
09:42 Priya Sharma: Ok thanks, we'll review the artifacts when they arrive and prioritize any blockers
09:47 Alex Moreno: Thanks everyone, I'll send the portal invite and a follow-up calendar invite for the evidence review call week of 2/24
09:54 Mark Ortiz: Thanks all
09:58 Dana Li: Thanks bye
10:02 End of transcript
